note: Big Bang to now, as the Weave tells it. Every statement carries a tag: established (textbook physics with data behind it), weave (our hypothesis, testable), open (unsolved or failed). Reusable by the Sky Map lesson system.

steps.title: Inflation
lines: established
A brief burst of accelerated expansion explains why the sky is so uniform and flat; its fingerprints are the nearly scale-invariant ripples in the CMB (n_s ≈ 0.965–0.973).
weave
The inflaton is the string coupling itself, τ₁, rolling on the SERAPIS-Λ plateau V ∝ (1 − 7.30 e^{−βψ}). It predicts n_s ≈ 0.9706 (fitted tilt) and r ≈ 5.4×10⁻⁴.
open
Primordial gravitational waves (r) are not yet detected; LiteBIRD and CMB-S4 will test r ~ 5×10⁻⁴.
steps.eq: V(τ₁) = V∞ (⅔ y∂_y ln E(τ₁, 3/2))² [1 + C(E − E_ρ)]

steps.title: The thread ties off
lines: weave
Inflation ends at the symmetric point ρ = e^{iπ/3}, where the potential is exactly zero. A residual Z₃ symmetry survives there.
weave
The 'Y-fork': slower fields can split off to the other knot, τ = i (neutrinos, later the dark thread).

steps.title: Reheating
lines: established
The inflaton's energy turns into a hot plasma of particles.
weave
Reheating temperature T_R ≈ 1.3×10⁹ GeV, with about 0.7% of the energy going to heat.

steps.title: The flavour ladder freezes
lines: weave
Heavy flavour fields settle on the rungs of the slip ladder: down quarks on rung 1, up quarks around rung 8 (5–14), charged leptons at the knot.
open
The quark sector is hosted, not predicted: the best model still misses m_s/m_b, V_cb and V_ub by 27–46%.

steps.title: Matter beats antimatter
lines: established
Today there is about one extra baryon per billion photons; the Standard Model alone cannot make that excess.
weave
Heavy neutrinos (10¹⁰–10¹² GeV) decay unevenly and leave a lepton excess, which becomes a baryon excess (leptogenesis); the same asymmetry also makes the dark matter.

steps.title: Electroweak transition
lines: established
The Higgs field switches on; W, Z and the fermions get their masses.

steps.title: Quarks bind into protons
lines: established
At about 150 MeV the quark–gluon plasma condenses into protons, neutrons and pions.

steps.title: Neutrinos decouple
lines: established
Neutrinos stop interacting and stream freely; today they form a background of 336 per cm³ at 1.95 K.
weave
Masses 0, 8.65 and 50.1 meV (Σ = 0.059 eV), suppressing small-scale structure by about 3.5%.

steps.title: The first nuclei
lines: established
Big Bang nucleosynthesis makes helium (Y_p ≈ 0.247) and deuterium (D/H ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵), matching observations.
open
Lithium-7 is about 3× over-predicted (the lithium problem); the Weave reproduces it but does not solve it.

steps.title: The CMB is released
lines: established
Atoms form, light streams free: the cosmic microwave background, a 2.7 K glow carrying the inflation ripples.

steps.title: Dark matter
lines: established
About 5× more matter than ordinary matter is dark; it shapes galaxies and the CMB peaks.
weave
Asymmetric dark matter (the sarion, 12.8 GeV) made from the same asymmetry as ordinary matter, cleaned up by a dark photon (the cassion).
open
No direct detection yet; LZ/XENONnT bounds apply.

steps.title: Galaxies and stars
lines: established
Gravity grows the ripples into galaxies, stars and planets.
open
The clumpiness S₈ was once in tension; with KiDS-Legacy (0.815) it is consistent, and does not separate models.

steps.title: Dark energy
lines: established
The expansion is accelerating; about 70% of today's energy is dark energy.
weave
The 'reverse thread': the same plateau shape at a tiny late height, a field (the Arthur field) now thawing toward τ = i; it fits DESI+DES-Y5 better than a constant, but meaningfully only on DES-Y5.
open
Why the dark-energy scale is 10⁻¹²⁰ in Planck units is not explained.

steps.title: The second knot
lines: weave
The dark thread comes to rest at the knot τ = i, mirroring how inflation ended at ρ: one thread, tied off at both ends.
